engine_meta.name: campus_social_research_analysis_engine
engine_meta.description: Maps user research goal, objectives, research questions, survey questions, database fields, calculations, and dashboard UI components for the Campus Social Experience Survey.
notes: This engine only uses already collected survey data.
No survey or DB schema changes are assumed.
Some research questions are only partially answerable with the current instrument.
Unsupported questions should be flagged for interviews or future research rounds.

research_goal.title: Social Initiation Gap Validation
research_goal.statement: To understand whether socially hesitant students on campus experience a meaningful social initiation gap where they want connection but struggle to begin it and to identify the conditions, contexts, and safeguards a digital solution would need in order to support low-pressure, judgment-free, spontaneous peer connection that improves belonging and social comfort on campus.

research_objectives.title: Validate whether the core problem truly exists for the target user on campus
research_objectives.description: Determine whether students want connection but struggle to initiate it, and how intense that problem is.

research_objectives.title: Identify who is most affected and define the primary user more clearly
research_objectives.description: Determine which student groups and psychological profiles are most likely to experience the social initiation gap.

research_objectives.title: Understand the barriers that prevent students from initiating peer interaction
research_objectives.description: Identify emotional, cognitive, and contextual blockers to starting conversations.

research_objectives.title: Understand the kinds of interaction settings that feel safest and easiest
research_objectives.description: Identify contexts and formats that make peer interaction easier, lower-pressure, and more natural.

research_objectives.title: Understand what makes a peer-connection experience feel safe, judgment-free, and trustworthy
research_objectives.description: Identify emotional safety factors and perceived conditions for comfortable interaction.

research_objectives.title: Investigate whether students need spontaneous connection, not just formal social opportunities
research_objectives.description: Assess whether students value spontaneous interaction opportunities and whether current social settings feel effortful.

research_objectives.title: Examine the role of digital mediation in lowering the barrier to first interaction
research_objectives.description: Assess whether online-first or digitally mediated interaction reduces initiation pressure.

research_objectives.title: Understand whether improved initiation could strengthen belonging over time
research_objectives.description: Examine whether students associate easier first interactions with greater social connectedness and belonging.

research_questions.question: Do students on campus want more peer connection but struggle to initiate conversation?

calculations.label: Average desire to expand social circle

research_questions.interpretation_rule: If desire is high and initiation difficulty is high, the social initiation gap exists.

research_questions.question: How common are feelings of hesitation, anxiety, overthinking, or fear of judgment when approaching new peers?
To what extent do students without an existing friend group feel lower belonging or higher social isolation?

calculations.label: Correlation between friend group and belonging

research_questions.question: Are there students who are socially inactive by preference, and others who want connection but feel blocked from starting it?
How intense is this problem in everyday campus life?
Which students are most likely to experience the social initiation gap: first-years, lateral entrants, off-campus students, day scholars, later-year introverts, or others?
limitations: Lateral entry / transfers are not directly captured in current demographics.
Introversion is not directly measured.

research_questions.question: What distinguishes students who are socially anxious from students who are simply introverted or selectively social?
limitations: This is a proxy model only.
Introversion is not directly measured in the current survey.

research_questions.question: Are students with few or no close campus friendships more likely to report hesitation in starting conversations?

calculations.label: Hesitation by close friend group level

research_questions.question: Do certain living situations or campus pathways make spontaneous connection easier or harder?
limitations: Campus pathways are not directly measured.

research_questions.question: What emotional and behavioral traits best describe the students who need this solution most?
What usually stops students from starting conversations with new people on campus?
How important are fear of rejection, fear of awkwardness, fear of judgment, low energy, and lack of common topics as blockers?
limitations: Fear of awkwardness is not directly asked as a standalone closed-ended item.

research_questions.question: What makes entering already-formed groups difficult?

calculations.label: Open text themes on formed groups

research_questions.question: When do students feel most anxious: before initiating, during the first interaction, or after it?
limitations: Temporal stage of anxiety is not captured in the current survey.

research_questions.question: How do students describe the emotional cost of making the first move?
limitations: The survey does not directly ask the phrase emotional cost.

research_questions.question: What kinds of settings make it easier for students to interact: classes, hostels, clubs, shared activities, mutual friends, or online spaces?
Do students feel more comfortable in small groups, one-on-one interactions, or larger social environments?
limitations: Group size preference is not directly asked.

research_questions.question: How important are shared interests, shared goals, or structured prompts in helping conversation begin naturally?
limitations: Shared goals and structured prompts are inferred from open text and preference items.

research_questions.question: Do students prefer interactions that are planned and guided, or those that feel more casual and spontaneous?
What makes an interaction feel low-pressure from the student's point of view?
What makes a new social interaction feel emotionally safe for students?
What makes students worry about being judged in campus social settings?
Would students prefer some anonymity or softer identity exposure at the beginning of interaction?
limitations: Anonymity or identity exposure preference is not directly asked.

research_questions.question: What kind of moderation, filtering, or community norms would make a digital space feel trustworthy?
limitations: Moderation and trust rules are not explicitly measured in the survey.

research_questions.question: What would make students feel unsafe, exposed, or pressured in a peer-connection platform?
Do students feel that existing campus social opportunities are too formal, effortful, or intimidating?
limitations: Existing opportunities are not directly rated with a closed-ended scale.

research_questions.question: Do students want more spontaneous ways to meet peers, rather than only events or structured sessions?
What would a digital bump into each other moment look like in campus life?
limitations: This requires concept-generation or interview data, not current survey data.

research_questions.question: How can a platform help first interactions happen naturally without making them feel forced?
limitations: Platform features are inferred rather than directly asked.

research_questions.question: Would students engage more with a solution that feels like part of daily life rather than another task or event?
limitations: Daily-life integration is not directly measured.

research_questions.question: Would students feel more comfortable initiating contact through a digital layer before interacting in person?
Does online-first or text-first interaction reduce the fear of starting a conversation?

calculations.label: Online comfort vs initiation anxiety correlation
Online comfort vs hesitation index correlation

limitations: Text-first specifically is not directly separated from online-first.

research_questions.question: What kind of digital scaffolding would help most: prompts, shared-interest matching, mutual context, icebreakers, or slow conversation formats?
limitations: Specific digital scaffolding features are not directly measured.

research_questions.question: At what point should a digital interaction move offline, if at all?
limitations: Offline transition timing is not captured.

research_questions.question: What makes digital support feel helpful rather than robotic or repetitive?
limitations: Perceptions of digital support quality are not measured.

research_questions.question: Do students believe that easier first interactions would improve their sense of belonging on campus?

calculations.label: Belonging vs desire for spontaneous interaction correlation

limitations: This is inferential because the survey does not directly ask whether easier first interactions improve belonging.

research_questions.question: What does feeling socially connected actually mean to students in their daily campus life?
limitations: Connectedness is not directly defined in a standalone open-ended question.

research_questions.question: What kinds of early interactions are most likely to turn into repeated contact or friendship?
limitations: Repeated contact is inferred from friendship formation context, not directly measured longitudinally.

research_questions.question: What would make students continue a connection after the first interaction?
limitations: Continuation after first interaction is not directly measured.

research_questions.question: How would students know that a solution is genuinely helping them belong, not just helping them chat once?
limitations: Success metrics for a future solution are not captured in the survey.

formula_definitions.mean: Average of one numeric field across filtered valid responses.
formula_definitions.composite_mean: Average of multiple numeric fields within each response, then average across responses.
formula_definitions.composite_mean_with_reverse_code: Reverse selected fields using reversed_value = scale_max + scale_min - original_value, then compute composite mean.
formula_definitions.frequency_distribution: Count and percentage per category or Likert option.
formula_definitions.group_mean_compare: Compute mean of a value field grouped by one categorical field.
formula_definitions.group_composite_mean: Compute composite mean grouped by one categorical field.
formula_definitions.correlation: Pearson or Spearman correlation between two numeric variables or a numeric variable and a composite score.
formula_definitions.difference_score: Subtract field_b from field_a to determine leaning or preference balance.
formula_definitions.rule_based_segmentation: Assign derived segment labels based on boolean conditions.
formula_definitions.multi_select_count: Count how many respondents selected each boolean multi-select option.
formula_definitions.multi_select_percentage: Percentage of respondents selecting each boolean multi-select option.
formula_definitions.boolean_prevalence: Percentage of valid responses where boolean field is true.
formula_definitions.hybrid_barrier_index: Combines counts from barrier checkboxes and mean from related scaled item.
formula_definitions.keyword_theme_extraction: Simple NLP keyword frequency and clustering from one open-text field.
formula_definitions.keyword_theme_extraction_dual_field: Simple NLP keyword frequency and clustering across two open-text fields.
formula_definitions.open_text_semantic_clustering: Embeddings or rule-based clustering of open-text responses into themes.
formula_definitions.multi_select_vs_numeric_compare: Compares numeric outcome across respondents who selected vs did not select each multi-select option.

ui_component_library.stacked_bar: Stacked bar chart for grouped proportions.
ui_component_library.radar_chart: Radar chart comparing multiple mean psychological variables.
ui_component_library.likert_distribution: Diverging stacked bar for Likert responses.
ui_component_library.heatmap: Matrix heatmap by field and average score.
ui_component_library.scatter_plot: Scatter plot with optional regression line.
ui_component_library.segment_pie_chart: Pie or donut for rule-based segments.
ui_component_library.segment_table: Table listing derived segment counts and percentages.
ui_component_library.summary_score_card: Large score tile with benchmark range.
ui_component_library.cross_tab_table: Cross-tabulation table with counts and means.
ui_component_library.segment_cards: Cards for derived personas or proxy profiles.
ui_component_library.ranked_table: Sorted table for barriers or contexts.
ui_component_library.combined_bar_and_score_card: Bar chart plus a headline score.
ui_component_library.theme_chip_list: Tag-like display of top extracted themes.
ui_component_library.theme_list: Ordered list of top open-text themes.
ui_component_library.theme_cluster_panel: Clustered theme visualization with optional quote examples.
ui_component_library.ranked_context_bar_chart: Bar chart of friendship context percentages.
ui_component_library.balance_distribution: Distribution of leaned_structured vs leaned_spontaneous vs balanced.
ui_component_library.design_opportunity_panel: Insight panel turning themes into design opportunities.
ui_component_library.persona_summary_panel: Persona/primary user summary with core stats.
ui_component_library.unsupported_notice: UI block that states current survey does not support answering this question directly.

validity_rules: Default dashboard filter should exclude suspect_submission = true.
All open-text analysis should anonymize text and avoid exposing identifiers.
If valid sample size for a subgroup is below 3, suppress detailed subgroup charts.
naming_rules: Use rq_id as the backend key for each analysis card.
Use calc_id as the backend key for each computed metric.
